title: Aft Lower Shell Skin — External Patch Repair Over the Bilge Line

issue.reason: Original issue of the external patch repair for the aft lower shell bilge line.

abstract: Permanent external patch repair for cracking or corrosion in the aft lower shell skin along the bilge line, with a fatigue life limit and a repeat ultrasonic inspection of the patch perimeter.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the static strength and the residual fatigue capability of the aft lower shell skin along the bilge line after crack or corrosion damage has been removed.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the extent of the damage by detailed visual inspection followed by an ultrasonic sweep of the surrounding area to a radius of at least 200 mm, because corrosion along the bilge line spreads under the protective treatment before it becomes visible. Damage that stays inside the allowable limits below may be blended out and left unrepaired provided the remaining thickness is measured and recorded. Damage that crosses a fastener row, that lies within 50 mm of an existing patch, or that has reduced the skin thickness by more than 15 per cent, is outside the scope of this repair and needs an engineering assessment. Record the damage position relative to the nearest frame station and the bilge outlet before removal, because the patch layout is set from the outlet position.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the damaged material by routing to a smooth oval with a minimum corner radius of 15 mm and blend the edges to the finish given in the standard practice. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the routed edge and repeat it after any further blending. Cut the external patch from 1.8 mm titanium sheet to the layout of repair drawing RD-53-31-12-902 and drill the fastener pattern using the patch as a template. Deburr every hole and apply the surface protection of ATA 51-20 to all new surfaces. Install the patch wet with sealant using rivets AES990489-7D on the two outer rows and rivets EN545167-02 on the inner row, to the pitch and edge distance given on the repair drawing. Install washers AGS334024-84 where the patch crosses an existing drain grommet position and check that the drain path is still clear with a water flow test. Where the patch crosses the stringer run D5331122551549, add the local packer shown on sheet 2 of the repair drawing. Restore the external finish to aerodynamic smoothness class B and re-apply the bilge protective compound over the whole repair area.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 18 000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment. Do a repeat ultrasonic inspection of the patch perimeter and of the routed edge every 4 500 flight cycles, and a detailed visual inspection of the bilge protective compound at every C-check. Any new indication inside the repair boundary makes the repair invalid and needs a new engineering assessment. Report the repair to Aeralis so that it is recorded against the aircraft and so that the drain path condition is tracked.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cracks up to 18 mm in length that do not cross a fastener row, are not closer than 15 mm to a fastener centre and are not closer than 50 mm to an existing patch. Corrosion pits up to 0.4 mm deep after blending, with the remaining skin thickness not less than 85 per cent of nominal. One damage area per skin bay.

title: Aft Lower Shell Skin — External Patch Repair Over the Bilge Line

issue.reason: Patch row count made a recorded output of the repair and the interaction with the joint doubler stated, so that the patch variant is known before a doubler change is planned.

abstract: Permanent external patch repair for cracking or corrosion in the aft lower shell skin along the bilge line, with a fatigue life limit, a repeat ultrasonic inspection of the patch perimeter and a recorded row count for later doubler work.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the static strength and the residual fatigue capability of the aft lower shell skin along the bilge line after crack or corrosion damage has been removed.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the extent of the damage by detailed visual inspection followed by an ultrasonic sweep of the surrounding area to a radius of at least 200 mm, because corrosion along the bilge line spreads under the protective treatment before it becomes visible. Record the damage position relative to the nearest frame station and the bilge outlet before removal, because the patch layout is set from the outlet position. Establish also whether the patch boundary will pick up the land of the longitudinal skin joint above the bilge line, and record the answer with the repair: that land carries the inner doubler, and the doubler can only be withdrawn into the compartment while the land is clear of patch fasteners.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the damaged material by routing to a smooth oval with a minimum corner radius of 15 mm and blend the edges to the finish given in the standard practice. Do a repeat ultrasonic inspection of the patch perimeter and of the routed edge every 4 500 flight cycles, and a detailed visual inspection of the bilge protective compound at every C-check. Any new indication inside the repair boundary makes the repair invalid and needs a new engineering assessment. Record the number of fastener rows in the patch and their position relative to the joint land on the aircraft structural record sheet. A patch whose outer row lands on the joint holds the inner doubler captive: the doubler cannot then be taken out from inside the compartment and a doubler change becomes a skin repair. Where a doubler change is being planned on a repaired aircraft, establish the patch variant by eddy current inspection of the joint land before the kit is ordered, as required by Service Bulletin CRN-53-1042. Report the repair to Aeralis so that it is recorded against the aircraft and so that the drain path condition is tracked.

Corrosion pits up to 0.4 mm deep after blending, with the remaining skin thickness not less than 85 per cent of nominal. One damage area per skin bay. A patch layout whose outer row falls in the longitudinal joint land is acceptable but must be recorded, because it makes the inner doubler captive.
